name: GM CCA - Philadelphia Parts Distribution Center, Langhorne PA

fieldNotes.facility: GM Customer Care & Aftersales (legacy SPO/Service Parts Operations) Philadelphia Parts Distribution Center at 200 Cabot Blvd E, Langhorne PA 19047. Rooftop geocode (40.193957,-74.834983) lands on the building; a single large single-story distribution warehouse confirmed by satellite, set back from US-1 in the Cabot industrial area off the NS Morrisville rail yard. Verified via business directories (193 employees, 267-580-2301) and UAW local listings (SPO Philadelphia).
fieldNotes.truckGate: Single private access drive curls SW off Cabot Blvd E into the property; long fenced, tree-buffered approach. No public Street View penetrates the drive (private), so the physical gate hardware is inferred from the controlled-access layout, not directly imaged.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No guard booth identifiable at the property entrance in satellite; access is via the long private drive. Treated as likely kiosk/app check-in (remoteGs) rather than a staffed booth; flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Access drive from Cabot Blvd to the truck court is several hundred feet and can stack 3+ trucks; the internal perimeter road around the building adds deep queuing room.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large paved truck court on the SE/south side between the dock apron and the rail buffer holds queued and dropped trailers inside the fence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Estimate ~34 dock positions along the single long SE building face (regular bay rhythm with trailers backed in across the dock apron); band 25-50.
fieldNotes.dropArea: A second row of free-standing nose-out drop trailers sits in the truck court ahead of the docked row; consistent with 25-50 dropped trailers. dropYard true.
fieldNotes.railServed: A rail spur enters the property from the SE and runs along the building (clearly visible at z20 near the NE/E corner) off the adjacent NS/Conrail Morrisville Yard. Spur present though primary inbound today is truck; flagged uncertain on current activity.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Edge-of-town industrial parcel beside US-1 and a rail yard, with farmland to the NW and a tree buffer around; judged Rural per rubric (small-town industrial leans Rural).
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Single dock bank on one building face; shipping and receiving share the same dock line.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified in imagery.
